summary: Defines S/MIME version 3.2, a consistent way to send and receive secure MIME data. It provides digital signatures for authentication and integrity and encryption for confidentiality. It is on the standards track and was replaced by RFC 8551.

eli5.summary: S/MIME lets you sign an email so people know it is from you, and seal it so only the right person can read it. This version describes the details. It was replaced by RFC 8551.

questions: how to sign and encrypt email with s/mime
